title: Adaptive de-escalation policy and runbook automation for pager noise reduction
creator: Maya Chen
description: Reduce on-call noise and mean time to resolution by introducing an adaptive de-escalation policy, consolidated runbooks for multi-region failover/circuit-breaker events, and automated incident response actions. This ticket will: 1) define adaptive alert thresholds tied to SLO burn rate and traffic patterns, 2) implement PagerDuty automation rules for suppressing duplicate alerts and auto-acknowledging low-impact bursts, 3) author canonical runbooks (failover, circuit-breaker trips, load-shedding) with step-by-step checks and automated remediation hooks, and 4) add observability dashboards and synthetic checks to validate the end-to-end flow. Objective: reduce duplicate pages by 60% in high-noise windows and cut context-switch time for on-call engineers by 25%.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive alerting policy deployed that ties alert severity to recent SLO burn-rate and request-per-second percentiles
PagerDuty rule set in prod that dedupes identical symptoms across regions and auto-acknowledges short-lived burst alerts (<90s) when traffic-normalizes
Three canonical runbooks merged to GitHub and linked in PagerDuty alerts: multi-region failover, circuit-breaker engagement, load-shedding escalation
Automated remediation playbooks for two low-risk actions (restart worker pool, toggle nonessential feature gate) implemented and tested in staging
Dashboards showing alert count, duplicate ratio, mean time to ack, mean time to resolve before/after rollout
Post-rollout synthetic test demonstrating suppression + auto-recovery path simulating high RPS spike with cache churn
implementation_steps: Design: document adaptive policy logic mapping SLO burn rate and 1m/5m/15m RPS percentiles to alert thresholds (contrib: SRE + Metrics) - Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Adaptive+Alerting
Config: add new alert rules to monitoring repo (monorepo path: monitoring/alerts/alerting_adaptive.yml) and feature flag behind toggle 'adaptive_alerting_v1'
PagerDuty: create new escalation policy 'Adaptive De-escalation' and add automation rules for dedupe and auto-ack. PD rule doc: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/rules/ADAPTIVE-DEESC
Runbooks: author runbooks in docs/runbooks/ with playbook steps and automated hooks that call internal remediation service (POST /ops/remediate)
Automation: implement two remediation handlers in ops-service with idempotent operations and feature gating; create unit + integration tests
Observability: add dashboard panels to Console under 'Oncall / Alerting Hygiene' and create a synthetic job 'alerting-suppression-test' in the synthetic-runner
Staging validation: execute end-to-end tests including synthetic spike, verify PagerDuty suppresses duplicates and automation performs expected actions
Canary rollout: enable adaptive policy for 10% traffic with rollout plan and rollback script; monitor key metrics for 48h
Full rollout and retrospective: enable for 100% on completion of canary and publish postmortem metrics to the team channel
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-suppression could hide real incidents. Mitigation: conservative thresholds and manual override in PagerDuty plus emergency bypass route
Risk: Automated remediations may cause cascading state. Mitigation: runbooks require safety checks and idempotent ops with dry-run option; limit automation to low-risk actions initially
Risk: Inconsistent cross-region symptom matching. Mitigation: enrich alerts with normalized fingerprints and request-trace IDs to enable deterministic dedupe
testing_plan: Unit tests for alarm-logic mapping functions and burn-rate calculation
Integration tests in staging that exercise PagerDuty automation rules and ops-service handlers
Chaos test: simulate region A saturation and verify alert grouping and canary failover procedure in the runbook executes without manual intervention
Load test: synthetic generator to create RPS spikes and cache churn to validate suppression window and TTL behavior
monitoring_and_metrics: Metric: alert_count_total (by alert_type, region) - aim: -60% duplicate alerts in burst windows
Metric: mttr_ack and mttr_resolve - target -25% reduction in ack time
Metric: automation_success_rate for remediations - target >95% in staging before prod enable
SLOs referenced: request_availability:99.95%, p95_latency:200ms - alerting sensitivity maps to 10% SLO burn in 10m window
